title: Grade 6 Science — Tue, Jun 02
description: Fibre to Fabric — Day 2 of 5: From cotton boll to yarn
subject: science

questions.question: The process of removing seeds from cotton fibres is called:
questions.explanation: Ginning is the process of separating cotton fibres from the seeds.

questions.question: The process of making yarn from fibres is called:
questions.explanation: Spinning is the process in which fibres are drawn out and twisted to make yarn.

questions.question: A simple hand device used for spinning yarn is the:
questions.explanation: The takli (hand spindle) and charkha (spinning wheel) are simple devices for spinning yarn by hand.

questions.question: Cotton is usually picked from the field by:
questions.explanation: Cotton bolls are picked from the plants by hand or by machines.

questions.question: In earlier days, ginning of cotton was mostly done by:
questions.explanation: Earlier, ginning was done by hand by combing the seeds out of the cotton; now machines are also used.

questions.question: Spinning twists fibres together mainly to make the yarn:
questions.explanation: Twisting the fibres together makes the yarn strong and forms a long continuous thread.

questions.question: Mahatma Gandhi encouraged people to spin yarn at home using the:
questions.explanation: Gandhiji promoted the charkha (spinning wheel) to make khadi and encourage self-reliance.

questions.question: The correct order of the first steps is:
questions.explanation: First cotton is picked, then ginned to remove seeds, then spun into yarn.

questions.question: After ginning, what remains to be spun into yarn?
questions.explanation: Ginning removes the seeds, leaving the cotton fibres to be spun into yarn.

questions.question: In a large textile factory, spinning is done on:
questions.explanation: In factories, large spinning machines spin huge amounts of yarn quickly.

questions.question: Cotton seeds removed during ginning are NOT wasted; they are used to make:
questions.explanation: Cotton seeds are used to make cooking oil and as feed for cattle.

questions.question: Why must fibres be made into yarn before making cloth?
options: Loose fibres cannot be woven into cloth directly
questions.explanation: Loose, short fibres must be spun into long, strong yarn before they can be woven or knitted into cloth.

questions.question: Which device is used to spin yarn but NOT to weave cloth?
questions.explanation: The charkha is used for spinning yarn; looms are used for weaving cloth.

questions.question: The fluffy white part inside a cotton boll is made up of:
questions.explanation: Inside the cotton boll are seeds covered with fluffy cotton fibres.

questions.question: Which step comes immediately AFTER spinning in making cloth?
options: Weaving or knitting the yarn into fabric
questions.explanation: After spinning produces yarn, the yarn is woven or knitted into fabric.
